Definition: from G3326 and G3992; to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite:--call (send) for.
BiblicalUsage: Cornelius is told to send men to Joppa and call for Peter, Paul calls the disciples together after the uproar at Ephesus, and Felix sends for Paul to hear him concerning the faith in Christ. The word is a summons from elsewhere, and Luke uses it whenever the gospel is about to cross a boundary.
TheologicalSignificance: I notice that every one of these sendings opened a door: Cornelius's household heard the gospel, the Ephesian disciples were embraced and sent on, and even Felix, who kept delaying, heard the faith in Christ.
